name: Bridge
tagline: A low-cost braille display that turns photos of notes and recorded lectures into raised pins.
problem: Deafblind students depend on interpreters, and commercial braille displays cost thousands of dollars, the team says.
solution: Images or audio are transcribed and summarised (Whisper, Claude), converted to braille patterns and driven onto a 3D-printed pin display by a rotating cam cylinder, stepper motors and an ESP32.
demo_moment: Team-described: photograph handwritten notes and feel the braille appear on the device.

why_it_stood_out.claim: A physical device costs a fraction of existing displays, the team says.

lessons: Hardware that a judge can touch makes an accessibility claim concrete.
